Let \(t=\frac{y}{z}\). The nonzero conditions give
\[
t\ne 0,\qquad 2t-3\ne 0 \implies t\ne \frac32.
\]
The expression becomes
\[
\frac{y^2}{xz}=\frac{t^2}{2t-3}.
\]
For \(0<t<\frac32\), we have \(2t-3<0\), while \(t^2>0\). As
\[
t\to \left(\frac32\right)^-,
\]
we get \(2t-3\to 0^-\), so
\[
\frac{t^2}{2t-3}\to -\infty.
\]
Thus the expression is unbounded below.

\[
\boxed{\text{No minimum exists; the expression is unbounded below.}}
\]
